title: Add a foreman focus verb to reveal and focus a terminal
body:
Add a `foreman focus [--project pN] tN` control verb: reveal and focus terminal tN exactly as clicking its row in the Sessions panel (or its tab chip) would. That means activating its tab when it is a back tab in a stack, restoring its window when minimized, and doing the same up the chain when its Project is itself a back tab or minimized on the desk. Find the act the Sessions panel pushes on a row click (src/panel.rs -> src/wm.rs) and reuse it: one home for "reveal and focus a terminal", not a second path.

WHY: since card czysfd, dispatched workers are back tabs and nothing outside the GUI can bring one forward. Card t5ohsm needed a throwaway, uncommitted shot hook (FOREMAN_SHOT_TAB_OVERFLOW) just to activate a tab for its screenshot. An orchestrator could also use this verb to jump to a worker that needs you.

SCOPE: in-app focus only. It must not raise the OS window or take the OS foreground. OUT OF SCOPE: opening the "+N" tab list from the CLI (that is pointer state), and any verb that changes layout.

This is a new control-plane verb, so read foreman-change-control first (wire compat v1, OpenReply skip_serializing_if) and follow src/control.rs's existing verb shape (request struct, client parse, --help, exit codes 0/1/2).

DONE WHEN:
- wm tests: a back tab becomes active and focused; a minimized window is restored, as a Sessions-panel click would; a terminal in a back-tab or minimized Project activates the desk tab, then the inner tab; afterwards exactly one terminal reads the keyboard (focus cascade); an unknown tN fails with exit 1 and changes nothing.
- control.rs parse and wire tests like the other verbs.
- Docs: the CLI verb list wherever foreman-run-and-operate points, plus foreman --help.
- Gate: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent.
